Learn By Doing
Overview

Perks and attributes level themselves through use. Swing a club and you train Clubs. Mine ore and you train Miner 69'r. Take hits in heavy armor and you train Heavy Armor.

Every attribute and most of its perks have a Learn By Doing track, so the way you play decides what your character becomes.

The progress bar on each row of the Skills window shows how close the next level is.
Leveling

Attributes rise from any action in their tree, so specialising in a few perks pulls the parent attribute up with it.

Combat perks want damage and kills with their own weapon. Gathering perks want the right tool on the right resource. Armor perks want you to take the hits.

Crafting skills run on their own, much longer curve, and crafting the same item over and over only pays once - variety counts.

Most awards are throttled, so grinding one action on the spot is slower than simply playing.
Changes

Buying perks and attributes with skill points is switched off, and no skill points are awarded on level up. Progression is earned in the field.

The Cost and Buy columns are gone from the Skills window for the same reason.

Everything else in the tree still applies. Level requirements, attribute caps and perk prerequisites are unchanged - Learn By Doing only changes how a level is paid for, not what it unlocks.
Learn By Doing
Overview

Perks and attributes level themselves through use. Swing a club and you train Clubs. Mine ore and you train Miner 69'r. Take hits in heavy armor and you train Heavy Armor.

Every attribute and most of its perks have a Learn By Doing track, so the way you play decides what your character becomes rather than how you spend points.

Each row of the Skills window carries a progress bar showing how close that skill is to its next level.
Leveling

Attributes rise from any action in their tree, so specialising in a few perks pulls the parent attribute up with it.

Combat perks want damage and kills with their own weapon. Gathering perks want the right tool on the right resource. Armor perks want you to take the hits while wearing that armor class.

Crafting skills run on their own, much longer curve. Crafting the same item over and over only pays once - the system remembers your previous craft, so variety counts. Repairing and scrapping earn as well, and starter gear that carries no schematic still counts up to level 10.

Most awards are throttled, so grinding a single action on the spot is slower than simply playing. Movement in particular is capped, however hard you run.
Decay

Skills you stop using will fade. Every Learn By Doing skill carries a hidden inactivity timer, and if it runs long enough with no related action, that skill drops a level.

Any action tied to the skill resets its timer to zero. A single swing, harvest or craft is enough - you do not have to level it again, only touch it.

The intent is that your character reflects how you actually play now, not everything you once did. Keeping a broad set of skills in occasional use costs very little; abandoning one entirely does.
Changes

Perks and attributes can no longer be bought with skill points, and no skill points are awarded on level up. Progression is earned in the field.

The Cost and Buy columns are gone from the Skills window, along with the points counter in its header, for the same reason.

Everything else in the tree still applies. Level requirements, attribute caps and perk prerequisites are unchanged - Learn By Doing only changes how a level is paid for, not what it unlocks.
